target.notes: Ant Design, mounted with default configuration using only components the library exports and no hand-written ARIA. Ant Design has no single combobox component: AutoComplete is the closest match to the APG editable-combobox pattern and is what is measured here. Its accordion is Collapse, and its menu is Dropdown with a menu prop.

assertions.title: The control that opens the dialog has an accessible name
assertions.rationale: A screen reader user hearing only "button" has no way to know what activating it will do.

assertions.title: The trigger can be reached with the Tab key
assertions.rationale: If Tab does not reach the trigger, a keyboard user cannot open the dialog at all.

assertions.title: Pressing Enter on the focused trigger opens the dialog
assertions.rationale: Mouse users can open it; if Enter does nothing, keyboard users are locked out of whatever the dialog contains.

assertions.title: The dialog exposes role=dialog or role=alertdialog
assertions.rationale: The role is what tells assistive technology this is a dialog, enabling its dialog-specific behaviour and announcements.

assertions.title: The dialog has an accessible name
assertions.rationale: On opening, a screen reader announces the dialog's name. Without one the user is told only that a dialog opened, with no indication of what it is for.

assertions.title: Focus moves into the dialog when it opens
assertions.rationale: If focus stays behind on the page, a keyboard or screen reader user has no idea the dialog appeared and must hunt for it.

assertions.title: Tab never reaches operable content behind the dialog
assertions.rationale: Content behind a modal is inert to a mouse user. If Tab escapes into it, a keyboard user ends up interacting with things they cannot see.
assertions.detail: Focus stayed within the dialog across six Tab presses.

assertions.title: Shift+Tab never reaches operable content behind the dialog
assertions.rationale: Backward traversal is routinely forgotten when forward traversal is handled, and it strands users just as badly.
assertions.detail: Focus stayed within the dialog across six Shift+Tab presses.

assertions.title: Tab never leaves the dialog, even briefly
assertions.rationale: A tab stop on nothing gives a keyboard user no feedback and no way to tell whether they have fallen out of the dialog. They have not, and can carry on, which is why this is not a blocker, but the APG asks Tab to cycle among the dialog's own elements.
assertions.detail: Focus left the dialog after 4 Tab presses.
assertions.expected: focus stays on the dialog's own elements throughout the cycle

assertions.title: Escape closes the dialog
assertions.rationale: Escape is the universally learned way out of a modal. Without it, a user who cannot find the close button is stuck.

assertions.title: Closing the dialog returns focus to the trigger
assertions.rationale: If focus is dropped to the top of the document on close, the user loses their place and has to tab back through the whole page.

assertions.title: Content behind the dialog is hidden from assistive technology
assertions.rationale: A modal is visually exclusive. If the page behind it is still in the accessibility tree, a screen reader user can read and operate content that a sighted user cannot reach.
assertions.detail: Background content is still exposed to assistive technology while the modal is open.
assertions.expected: hr-outside-content hidden from the accessibility tree (aria-hidden, inert, or equivalent)
assertions.actual: hr-outside-content still present and not ignored

assertions.title: The close control has an accessible name
assertions.rationale: Close buttons are frequently icon-only. Without a name, the way out of the dialog is announced as an unlabelled button.
